ab-wheel-rollout.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
cues: Set up: Use a stable surface and begin with a short reach. Establish trunk control before extending the limbs farther.
Movement: Kneel with the wheel below your shoulders; brace your trunk and roll forward.
Control: Reach only as far as you can control your lower back, then roll back.
Brace: Keep the abdomen firm and breathe without letting the ribs flare. The limb movement should not drag the trunk out of position.
Reach: Extend deliberately and stop before your back arches or pelvis rotates. Shortening the lever is a useful way to reduce difficulty.
Return: Bring the limbs back under control and reset your brace. Maintain the same stable trunk rather than rushing between repetitions.
avoid: Avoid letting your lower back sag or pulling back by sitting onto your heels.
Excessive reach: Do not extend farther than you can return without changing trunk position. Reduce the range first.
Breath holding: Do not turn a controlled core drill into a prolonged breath hold. Keep breathing and shorten the set if needed.
Fast switching: Do not let speed conceal a loss of back or pelvis control. Pause in the starting position before the next repetition.

barbell-back-squat.name: Barbell Back Squat
cues: Set up: Choose a stance and toe angle that let your knees and hips move comfortably. Rehearse the movement before adding load.
Movement: Set your feet at a comfortable width; brace and bend your hips and knees together.
Control: Keep your whole foot planted, squat to a controlled depth, then stand.
Foot pressure: Keep your heel and both sides of the forefoot supported. Let the knees follow the direction of the toes.
Brace: Firm your abdomen before descending and keep the load balanced over your base of support as hips and shoulders rise together.
Depth: Use the deepest repeatable range you can control without losing balance. Knee travel past the toes is not automatically an error.
Rack setup: Set the hooks and safety bars for this lift and test them with an unloaded bar. Plan the unrack and rerack before loading.
avoid: Avoid losing foot contact or letting the load pull you out of balance.
Knees collapsing: If the knees suddenly fall inward and the feet roll, reduce the load or depth and rebuild a stable descent.
Rushing the bottom: Do not drop into a depth you cannot reverse under control. Keep tension as you change direction.
Hips shooting up: If your hips rise before your chest and you fold forward, use less resistance and push the floor away evenly.

barbell-bench-press.name: Barbell Bench Press
cues: Set up: Center yourself on secure support, take a full grip and organize the load before the first rep. Start with a manageable weight.
Movement: Set a stable position on the bench and keep wrists over forearms.
Control: Lower the weight toward your chest with control, then press it back up.
Grip: Keep the weight over the forearm rather than folded back across the wrist. Choose an elbow path you can control comfortably.
Lowering: Guide the load to a repeatable bottom position. Keep the upper back supported and resist a sudden drop in the last part.
Press: Push smoothly through the hands while maintaining your support. Keep both sides moving evenly rather than twisting to finish.
Failed-rep plan: Set appropriate rack safeties and use a competent spotter when needed. Check the protection before pressing; do not rely on recovering a trapped bar.
Bench support: Keep the feet secure on the floor or bench supports and the upper back settled on the pad. Reset your breath and brace between reps.
avoid: Avoid bouncing the weight or losing control of your shoulder position.
Grip mismatch: Do not force a grip width that makes the wrists fold or shoulders uncomfortable. Adjust the grip with a light load first.
Changing support: Do not lift your pelvis or slide along the support to complete a difficult rep. Stop before the position breaks down.
Uncontrolled finish: Do not slam the weights together or into the rack. Stabilize them and return them deliberately after the set.

barbell-front-squat.name: Barbell Front Squat
cues: Set up: Choose a stance and toe angle that let your knees and hips move comfortably. Rehearse the movement before adding load.
Movement: Rest the bar across the front shoulders; keep elbows lifted and brace.
Control: Squat between your legs with full-foot contact, then stand without losing the rack position.
Foot pressure: Keep your heel and both sides of the forefoot supported. Let the knees follow the direction of the toes.
Brace: Firm your abdomen before descending and keep the load balanced over your base of support as hips and shoulders rise together.
Depth: Use the deepest repeatable range you can control without losing balance. Knee travel past the toes is not automatically an error.
Rack setup: Set the hooks and safety bars for this lift and test them with an unloaded bar. Plan the unrack and rerack before loading.
Front rack: Let the shoulders carry the bar with elbows lifted. Do not try to hold the entire load in bent wrists.
avoid: Avoid letting the bar roll off the shoulders or forcing a depth you cannot control.
Knees collapsing: If the knees suddenly fall inward and the feet roll, reduce the load or depth and rebuild a stable descent.
Rushing the bottom: Do not drop into a depth you cannot reverse under control. Keep tension as you change direction.
Hips shooting up: If your hips rise before your chest and you fold forward, use less resistance and push the floor away evenly.

barbell-hip-thrust.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
cues: Set up: Choose secure support and foot placement that let you lift without sliding. Center and stabilize any external load before starting.
Movement: Support your upper back on the bench, plant your feet, and secure the load over your hips.
Control: Lift your hips until your trunk and thighs align; lower with control.
Hip drive: Press the feet down and lift from the hips. Keep your ribs from flaring as the pelvis rises.
Top position: Finish by squeezing the glutes with the trunk controlled. Stop when the hips are extended rather than arching to get higher.
Foot position: Adjust the feet if you cannot keep stable pressure. Maintain the same pelvis orientation and controlled path on each rep.
avoid: Avoid arching your lower back to lift the load higher.
Sliding support: Do not continue if the bench, back support or feet shift. Unload and reposition the setup first.
Head thrown back: Keep the neck comfortable rather than throwing your head backward to finish the lift.
Uneven hips: If one side rises or twists first, reduce the load or range and restore an even, controlled hip movement.

barbell-romanian-deadlift.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
cues: Set up: Begin tall with softly bent knees and a firm trunk. Practice sending the hips backward before increasing resistance.
Movement: Soften your knees, brace, and move your hips back while keeping the weight close.
Control: Lower to a controlled hamstring stretch, then extend your hips to stand.
Hip path: Think of closing a door with your hips. The torso tips as a result of the hinge while your back shape stays controlled.
Bottom position: Stop when further reach would change your back or pelvis position. Reaching the floor is not the goal.
Return: Push through the supporting foot or feet and bring the hips forward to stand. Finish tall without adding a backward lean.
avoid: Avoid reaching lower by rounding your back or turning it into a squat.
Knee drift: Do not keep bending the knees to gain depth and turn the hinge into a squat. Keep the knee bend modest and repeatable.
Neck extension: Do not lift your chin to stare ahead as you hinge. Let your gaze move naturally with your torso.
Lost brace: If the trunk position changes suddenly, shorten the range or use less resistance instead of forcing the next rep.

barbell-row.name: Barbell Row
cues: Set up: Choose support or a hip-hinge position you can hold for the set. Take a secure grip and test the pulling path with light resistance.
Movement: Hinge at the hips and brace your torso with the weight hanging below you.
Control: Pull toward your lower ribs or waist, then lower until your arms extend.
Elbow path: Pull the elbows toward the intended row target while keeping the wrists aligned. Grip width and elbow angle may vary with the exercise.
Shoulder movement: Allow the shoulder blades to glide as the arms reach and pull; do not squeeze them rigidly throughout the rep.
End position: Finish the pull before you have to rock the torso or roll the shoulders forward. Return through the same controlled path.
avoid: Avoid standing upright on each rep or jerking the weight.
Shrugging the pull: Do not raise the shoulders toward the ears to move the handle. Reduce load and restore the intended elbow path.
Changing torso angle: Do not repeatedly stand up or rock backward to finish the row. Use resistance you can pull from a stable base.
Excessive reach: Do not let the returning load pull your whole body out of position. Let the arms reach while retaining trunk control.

bulgarian-split-squat.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
cues: Set up: Leave enough width between your feet for balance rather than standing on a tightrope. Use light resistance while finding your stride.
Movement: Set your rear foot on a stable bench and plant the front foot for balance.
Control: Bend the front knee to lower, then push through the front foot to rise.
Front leg: Keep the front heel and forefoot supported; allow the knee to follow the toes as your hips lower between your feet.
Torso: A controlled forward lean can be appropriate. Keep your trunk braced instead of forcing an upright torso by arching your back.
Balance: Rise mainly through the front leg while the rear leg helps balance. Reset your feet if the next rep starts from an unstable stance.
Rear-foot support: Use a stable support that lets you balance without forcing the back hip. The front leg supplies most of the lifting effort.
avoid: Avoid wobbling on the platform or dropping the back knee.
Stride mismatch: Do not keep a step length that makes your heel lift or pelvis twist. Adjust the stance before adding weight.
Knee impact: Keep the rear knee from hitting the floor or platform. Shorten the range if you cannot control the last part of the descent.
Uneven reps: Do not rush the less stable side or twist to finish it. Use a controllable load and range on each leg.

cable-lateral-raise.name: Cable Lateral Raise
cues: Set up: Use light resistance and stable support. Start with a soft elbow bend and find a shoulder path you can repeat comfortably.
Movement: Start with your arms low and elbows softly bent.
Control: Raise your arms out to a comfortable shoulder height, then lower slowly.
Lead: Move the upper arms along the intended raise path rather than flicking the wrists. Keep your neck relaxed.
Shoulder motion: Allow the shoulder blades to move with the arms. Do not force them permanently downward while lifting.
Range: Raise only while the trunk and arm path stay controlled; return deliberately instead of letting the weight fall.
avoid: Avoid using an exaggerated neck shrug or torso swing to lift the load.
Momentum: Do not bounce the knees or swing the torso to start the raise. Lower the resistance and move from the shoulders.
Wrist steering: Do not force the wrists into an exaggerated thumbs-down position. Keep a comfortable grip and wrist alignment.
Changing lever: Do not repeatedly bend the elbows to finish heavy reps. Keep the arm shape consistent or reduce the load.

Control: Pull the load toward your torso with your elbows, then let your arms extend slowly.
Elbow path: Pull the elbows toward the intended row target while keeping the wrists aligned. Grip width and elbow angle may vary with the exercise.
Shoulder movement: Allow the shoulder blades to glide as the arms reach and pull; do not squeeze them rigidly throughout the rep.

avoid: Avoid jerking with your trunk or letting the load pull you forward.
Shrugging the pull: Do not raise the shoulders toward the ears to move the handle. Reduce load and restore the intended elbow path.
Changing torso angle: Do not repeatedly stand up or rock backward to finish the row. Use resistance you can pull from a stable base.
Excessive reach: Do not let the returning load pull your whole body out of position. Let the arms reach while retaining trunk control.

conventional-barbell-deadlift.name: Deadlift
cues: Set up: Bring the load close, take a secure grip and remove slack before lifting. Set the start height so you can brace in balance.
Movement: Set your stance and grip so the weight stays close; brace before lifting.
Control: Push through the floor to stand tall, then lower by bending hips and knees.
Leg drive: Push the floor away as hips and shoulders rise together. Keep the arms long; they hold the load rather than curl it.
Load path: Keep the weight close to your legs while leaving clearance for the knees. Finish standing tall with hips and knees extended.
Reset: Lower with a controlled hip hinge and knee bend. Re-establish your grip, balance and brace before each new pull.
avoid: Avoid yanking the weight from the floor or leaning back at the top.
Early hip rise: If the hips shoot up while the load stays still, reset your start position and reduce the weight.
Arm pull: Do not bend the elbows or jerk with the shoulders to break the weight free. Build tension before pushing through the legs.
Bouncing: Do not rebound the weight off the floor or rack supports. Settle it and regain control before the next rep.

dead-bug.name: Dead Bug
cues: Set up: Use a stable surface and begin with a short reach. Establish trunk control before extending the limbs farther.
Movement: Lie on your back with arms up and hips and knees bent to about 90 degrees.
Control: Extend one arm and the opposite leg, return, then switch sides.
Brace: Keep the abdomen firm and breathe without letting the ribs flare. The limb movement should not drag the trunk out of position.

Return: Bring the limbs back under control and reset your brace. Maintain the same stable trunk rather than rushing between repetitions.

Grip: Keep the weight over the forearm rather than folded back across the wrist. Choose an elbow path you can control comfortably.

dumbbell-hammer-curl.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
cues: Set up: Choose the intended grip and secure any bench or arm support. Start with resistance you can curl without moving the trunk.
Movement: Hold the weights with palms facing inward and elbows near your sides.
Control: Curl without rotating your wrists, then lower slowly.
Elbow movement: Bend at the elbow while keeping the upper arm reasonably steady in the position for this variation.
Wrist: Keep the wrist aligned with the forearm. Any grip rotation should be deliberate rather than caused by the weight pulling your hand.
Return: Extend the elbow smoothly through a comfortable range. Retain control near the bottom rather than dropping into the stretch.
avoid: Avoid swinging your torso or letting your wrists fold.
Trunk swing: Do not lean back or drive with the hips to start the curl. Lower the load and keep the same support position.
Elbow drift: Do not let the upper arm suddenly travel forward to finish heavy reps. Use a range and load you can control.
Bottom bounce: Do not rebound out of an extended elbow, especially on a supported curl. Slow the last part of the return.

Movement: Place your whole working foot on a stable platform.
Control: Stand through that leg, then step down slowly and with balance.
Working leg: Put the entire lead foot on top before pushing. Keep the knee following the toes while you lift your body.

Descent: Lower the trailing foot to the floor under control while the lead foot stays supported. Reset before switching legs.
avoid: Avoid springing off the trailing foot or stepping onto an unstable box.

cues: Set up: Secure the cable or band near face height and take a stable stance. Use resistance you can pull without leaning back.
Movement: Set the cable or band around face height and take a stable stance.
Control: Pull toward your face with elbows opening outward, then return slowly.
Pull: Bring the ends toward the sides of the face as the elbows open outward. Keep the wrists comfortable rather than forcing rotation.
Trunk: Keep your chest steady and abdomen firm. Move the arms and shoulder blades while the rest of the body remains balanced.
Return: Let the arms extend along the same line while keeping control of the cable or band tension.
avoid: Avoid leaning back or snapping the handle toward your face.
Low pull: Do not drag the handle toward the stomach as if doing a row. Adjust anchor height and use the intended face-height path.
Forced rotation: Do not crank the hands back farther than the shoulders can control. Use a comfortable end position.
Whole-body pull: Do not sway backward to start each repetition. Reduce the resistance and keep the stance steady.

farmer-carry.name: Farmer Carry
cues: Set up: Clear a level walking route and choose a load you can lift and set down deliberately. Check grip before taking the first step.
Movement: Lift the load securely and stand tall with your trunk braced.
Control: Walk with even steps while keeping the weight under control.
Posture: Keep the ribs controlled and head over the trunk. Let the arms hang long without forcing the shoulders into a rigid squeeze.
Steps: Walk with short, even steps and keep the load from striking your legs. Make turns slowly with space for the weights.
Finish: Stop before your grip opens or posture deteriorates. Place the load down through a controlled hip and knee bend.
avoid: Avoid leaning heavily to one side or rushing with an insecure grip.
Side bend: Do not lean heavily toward or away from a one-sided load. Reduce weight and keep the trunk centered.
Rushed turns: Do not pivot quickly with swinging weights. Slow down and turn with several controlled steps.
Grip gamble: Do not continue until you must drop the weights unexpectedly. End the carry while you can still set them down.

Movement: Hang from a secure bar with your shoulders and trunk engaged.
Control: Raise your knees or legs toward your torso, then lower slowly.
Trunk: Engage the shoulders and abdomen before lifting. Raise the legs while controlling the pelvis rather than starting a body swing.
Height: Use a height you can reach without losing the hang or throwing the head backward. Straight legs create a harder lever.
Lowering: Bring the legs down deliberately and settle any swing before repeating. Step down before your grip fails.
avoid: Avoid swinging to lift your legs or dropping into the bottom.
Swing start: Do not kick the legs backward to create momentum for a controlled raise. Reduce range or bend the knees.
Sudden drop: Do not let the legs fall and yank the shoulders at the bottom. Keep control of the full return.
Grip failure: Do not keep hanging when the hands begin slipping. Use a safe step down and rest before another set.

jump-rope.name: Jump Rope
cues: Set up: Use a level, non-slip landing surface and clear the surrounding area. Start with low jumps you can land on steadily.
Movement: Turn the rope mainly from your wrists and keep your jumps low.
Control: Land softly with a steady rhythm and relaxed knees.
Landing: Let ankles, knees and hips soften to absorb the landing. Keep the knees following the feet rather than suddenly collapsing inward.
Rhythm: Regain balance before the next jump. Increase speed or height only while landings remain quiet and controlled.
Fatigue: End the set when foot placement or landing control deteriorates. Quality landings matter more than keeping a fast pace.
Rope rhythm: Turn the rope mainly with the wrists and use only enough jump height to clear it. Keep elbows near the body and land lightly.
avoid: Avoid jumping much higher than needed or landing stiff-legged.
Stiff landing: Do not keep the knees rigid on contact. Reduce jump height and rehearse a softer landing.
Uncontrolled repetition: Do not bounce into another jump before regaining balance. Pause and reset when necessary.
Unsafe surface: Do not jump on a wet, unstable or crowded area. Fix the landing space before starting.

cues: Set up: Clear the area and use a kettlebell you can grip securely. Learn the hip hinge and swing before attempting a faster or overhead variation.
Movement: Hike the kettlebell between your legs and drive your hips forward.
Control: Let the bell float from hip power, then hinge as it swings back.
Power: Drive through the feet and extend the hips; the arms guide the bell. Keep the bell close during the backswing.
Timing: Let the returning bell approach your body before hinging back. Keep your abdomen firm as you stand tall at the finish.

avoid: Avoid lifting it mainly with your arms or leaning back at the top.

Loose grip: Do not keep going when sweat, fatigue or a damaged handle makes the grip unreliable. Set the bell down and reset.
Chasing height: Do not use a bigger back arch or shoulder yank to raise the bell higher. Reduce the load and restore hip-driven timing.

kneeling-cable-crunch.name: Kneeling Cable Crunch
cues: Set up: Find a stable position with comfortable neck support or hand placement. Begin with a small, deliberate trunk curl.
Movement: Kneel facing the high cable with the rope held near your head.
Control: Curl your ribs toward your pelvis, then return slowly.
Abdominal action: Bring the ribs and pelvis closer through the intended curl. Avoid making limb movement the only visible action.
Breathing: Exhale through the effort without yanking the head. Keep the movement smooth rather than holding a tense neck position.
Return: Uncurl gradually and reset before the next rep. Use a range that keeps the trunk movement controlled.
avoid: Avoid pulling mainly with your arms or swinging your hips.
Neck pull: Do not pull the head forward with the hands or handle. Keep the neck comfortable and let the trunk do the work.
Momentum: Do not throw the arms, legs or torso to complete the curl. Slow down and reduce resistance or lever length.
Losing the return: Do not drop back into the starting position. Shorten the set when you cannot control the uncurling.

lat-pulldown.name: Lat Pulldown
cues: Set up: Secure the seat, knee support or band anchor. Choose a grip that allows a comfortable overhead reach without losing your base.
Movement: Set a stable seat or stance and take a comfortable grip on the handle.
Control: Pull toward your upper chest, then let your arms rise slowly.
Pull: Draw the elbows down toward the sides while the chest stays steady. Follow the handle path without yanking with the hands.
Shoulders: Allow the shoulder blades to move upward on the return and downward on the pull. Keep the neck comfortable.
Range: Finish before the shoulders roll forward or the trunk swings back. Control the return to a comfortable long-arm position.
avoid: Avoid throwing your torso backward or pulling behind your neck.
Rowing the handle: Do not lean far back to convert the pull into a row. Reduce resistance and restore the downward elbow path.
Neck avoidance: Do not duck the head or pull behind the neck. Bring the handle in front along a comfortable path.
Unsecured base: Do not continue if the thighs lift, knees slide or band anchor shifts. Fix the setup before the next pull.

leg-extension.name: Leg Extension
cues: Set up: Adjust the backrest so your knee lines up with the pivot. Rest the roller on the lower shin, above the ankle joint.
Movement: Align your knees with the machine pivot and place the pad above your ankles.
Control: Straighten your knees smoothly, then lower the lever with control.
Support: Sit back against the pad and hold the handles. Keep your thighs supported as the lower legs move.
Top position: Straighten the knee through a comfortable range and pause briefly without throwing the lever into its stop.
Return: Follow the same path back slowly enough to control the stack. Keep the selected weight from pulling you out of the seat.
avoid: Avoid kicking the weight up or letting the stack slam.
Misaligned pivot: Do not compensate for a poorly adjusted seat by sliding forward. Stop and adjust the machine before the set.
Torso swing: If you rock backward to lift the pad, lower the weight and keep your trunk supported.
Forced range: Do not chase a machine stop that forces an uncomfortable knee position. Use a range you can reverse smoothly.

leg-press.name: Leg Press
cues: Set up: Adjust the back and shoulder supports to fit you. Find the safety stops and release mechanism before moving the load.
Movement: Set a stable foot position on the platform and keep hips against the seat.
Control: Lower the sled as far as you can keep your pelvis stable, then press it away.
Feet: Place the whole foot securely on the platform. Choose spacing that lets the knees follow the feet throughout the machine path.
Range: Stop the descent before your pelvis rolls away from the pad or your feet lose support; more depth is not useful without control.
Finish: Extend your legs smoothly without snapping the knees. Re-engage the catches before taking your feet off the platform.
avoid: Avoid letting your pelvis lift or snapping your knees straight.
Hands pushing knees: Keep hands on the machine grips instead of using your arms to force a rep. Reduce the resistance when needed.
Uneven pressure: Do not let one foot slide or one leg take over. Reset your stance before continuing.
Uncontrolled release: Do not unlock a sled you cannot support or continue when you cannot reach its catches. Test the mechanism with a light load.

lying-leg-curl.name: Lying Leg Curl
cues: Set up: Secure the resistance and support your trunk before starting. Try a light repetition to check that the knee can bend freely.
Movement: Align your knee with the machine pivot and secure the pads.
Control: Bend your knee to pull the pad toward you, then return slowly.
Knee movement: Draw the heel toward the back of the thigh while keeping the thigh and pelvis steady against their support.
Range: Curl only as far as you can without lifting your hips or changing your back position; contact with the glutes is not required.
Return: Let the knee extend smoothly while keeping control of the resistance. Maintain secure contact with the pad, cuff or dumbbell.
avoid: Avoid lifting your hips off the support or letting the stack slam.
Back arch: If your lower back arches to finish the curl, reduce resistance and stop the rep before the hips lift.
Rushed return: Do not let the resistance yank the leg straight. Lower slowly enough to keep the knee movement controlled.
Loose contact: Stop if the pad, ankle attachment or dumbbell slips. Reset the attachment instead of trying to catch it mid-rep.

one-arm-dumbbell-row.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
cues: Set up: Choose support or a hip-hinge position you can hold for the set. Take a secure grip and test the pulling path with light resistance.
Movement: Hinge at the hips and brace your torso with the weight hanging below you.
Control: Pull toward your lower ribs or waist, then lower until your arms extend.
Elbow path: Pull the elbows toward the intended row target while keeping the wrists aligned. Grip width and elbow angle may vary with the exercise.
Shoulder movement: Allow the shoulder blades to glide as the arms reach and pull; do not squeeze them rigidly throughout the rep.
End position: Finish the pull before you have to rock the torso or roll the shoulders forward. Return through the same controlled path.
avoid: Avoid standing upright on each rep or jerking the weight.
Shrugging the pull: Do not raise the shoulders toward the ears to move the handle. Reduce load and restore the intended elbow path.
Changing torso angle: Do not repeatedly stand up or rock backward to finish the row. Use resistance you can pull from a stable base.
Excessive reach: Do not let the returning load pull your whole body out of position. Let the arms reach while retaining trunk control.

overhead-cable-triceps-extension.name: Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
cues: Set up: Secure your support and use a full grip. Establish a comfortable upper-arm position with light resistance before bending the elbows.
Movement: Hold the load overhead with elbows aimed generally forward and trunk braced.
Control: Bend your elbows to lower the load, then extend them under control.
Upper arms: Keep the upper arms reasonably steady while the elbows bend and extend. Their angle may vary with the chosen setup.
Trunk: Keep the ribs controlled rather than arching the back for more reach. Hold the load securely throughout the lowered position.
Extension: Extend smoothly and reverse before the weight pulls your elbows out of position. Keep a comfortable wrist alignment.
avoid: Avoid arching your lower back or letting the load fall behind you.
Head clearance: Do not lower the load so quickly that it threatens head contact. Use a controllable path and lighter resistance.
Elbow forcing: Do not squeeze the elbows into an uncomfortable narrow position. Use spacing that permits smooth movement.
Arm swing: Do not turn the extension into a pullover or press to finish heavy reps. Reduce load and regain elbow control.

pallof-press.name: Pallof Press
cues: Set up: Secure the cable or band at chest height and stand sideways to the anchor. Choose resistance that allows a stable stance.
Movement: Stand sideways to the cable or band with the handle at chest height.
Control: Press your hands forward without rotating, then bring them back.
Press: Extend the hands forward from the chest while the ribs and pelvis continue facing the same direction.
Hold: Resist the sideways pull rather than trying to rotate against it. Keep pressure through both feet and breathe.
Return: Bring the hands back to the chest deliberately. Reset your stance before switching which side faces the anchor.
avoid: Avoid twisting toward the anchor or leaning to counter the load.
Body turn: Do not let the hands pull the torso toward the anchor. Reduce tension or stand closer with a band.
Side lean: Do not lean away to balance a weight you cannot resist. Keep the trunk centered over the feet.
Loose anchor: Do not use a band attached to a movable or unreliable object. Check the attachment before tensioning it.

pec-deck-fly.name: Pec Deck Fly
cues: Set up: Secure your stance or bench position and select light resistance. Find a comfortable starting arm position before opening wider.
Movement: Adjust the seat so your arms meet the pads or handles at chest height.
Control: Bring your arms together, then open them slowly.
Arm arc: Keep a small, fairly consistent elbow bend as the upper arms move. Think of bringing the arms together rather than pushing the hands.
Stretch: Stop opening before the load pulls the shoulders out of control. A larger stretch is not automatically a better repetition.
Closing: Follow the same arc back without banging handles or dumbbells together. Keep the trunk position steady.
Machine fit: Adjust the seat so the handles or arm pads match your shoulder height. Keep the torso supported and follow the machine’s comfortable arc.
avoid: Avoid letting the machine pull your shoulders far behind you.
Changing elbow bend: Do not repeatedly bend and straighten the elbows to turn the fly into a press. Lower the resistance if needed.
Forced bottom: Do not let gravity or the cable pull the arms farther back than you can reverse smoothly.
Torso swing: Do not rock your body or lift off the support to close the arms. Restore a stable setup with less load.

pull-ups.name: Pull-Ups
cues: Set up: Check the bar and arrange a stable way to get on and off it. Use assistance if you cannot control both the pull and descent.
Movement: Hang from a secure bar with a comfortable grip and a braced trunk.
Control: Pull your body toward the bar, then lower with control.
Pull: Think of drawing the elbows down toward the ribs as the body rises. Let the shoulder blades move rather than forcing them still.
Body position: Brace lightly and keep the legs quiet. Finish at a height you can reach without thrusting the chin forward.
Descent: Lower until the arms reach a comfortable extended position while keeping shoulder and grip control.
avoid: Avoid swinging to clear the bar or craning your neck for extra height.
Kipping unintentionally: Do not kick or swing to replace a controlled strength rep. Increase assistance instead.
Neck reach: Do not crane the neck just to get the chin over the bar. Keep the head aligned with the moving torso.
Dropping: Do not fall into the bottom or release a failing grip from height. Use a controlled step down and stop before grip failure.

weighted-pull-ups.name: Weighted Pull-Ups
cues: Set up: Check the bar and arrange a stable way to get on and off it. Use assistance if you cannot control both the pull and descent.
Movement: Hang from a secure bar with a comfortable grip and a braced trunk.
Control: Pull your body toward the bar, then lower with control.
Pull: Think of drawing the elbows down toward the ribs as the body rises. Let the shoulder blades move rather than forcing them still.
Body position: Brace lightly and keep the legs quiet. Finish at a height you can reach without thrusting the chin forward.
Descent: Lower until the arms reach a comfortable extended position while keeping shoulder and grip control.
avoid: Avoid swinging to clear the bar or craning your neck for extra height.
Kipping unintentionally: Do not kick or swing to replace a controlled strength rep. Increase assistance instead.
Neck reach: Do not crane the neck just to get the chin over the bar. Keep the head aligned with the moving torso.
Dropping: Do not fall into the bottom or release a failing grip from height. Use a controlled step down and stop before grip failure.

push-press.name: Push Press
cues: Set up: Rack the weight near the shoulders and brace in a balanced standing position. Learn a strict press before adding leg drive.
Movement: Hold the weight at your shoulders; dip a little by bending hips and knees.
Control: Drive through your legs and finish by pressing overhead; lower under control.
Dip: Bend hips and knees slightly while keeping the weight supported and torso tall. Keep pressure through the whole foot during the dip.
Drive: Extend the legs decisively, then continue pressing with the arms. Let the shoulder blades move as the weight travels overhead.
Reset: Stabilize overhead, guide the load back to the shoulders and absorb it with a controlled knee bend before repeating.
avoid: Avoid a deep forward-folding dip or pressing from an unstable stance.
Forward dip: Do not tip the torso forward and lose the rack position during the dip. Reduce load and rehearse a balanced dip.
Early arm press: Do not start with the arms before the legs drive. Coordinate the dip and drive before adding weight.
Uncontrolled catch: Do not let the returning load crash onto the shoulders. Stop the set when you cannot receive it steadily.

push-ups.name: Push-Ups
cues: Set up: Use a non-slip surface or secure handles. Choose a support height that lets you lower and press with a firm trunk.
Movement: Place hands securely and hold a straight, braced line from head to heels.
Control: Lower your chest toward your support, then press away with control.
Body line: Brace the abdomen and glutes; let the shoulders, hips and legs travel together rather than peeling the chest up first.
Hands and elbows: Spread pressure through the hands and choose a comfortable elbow path. Keep the neck in line with the trunk.
Top position: Push the support away and let the shoulder blades move naturally. Finish each rep in a stable plank before descending again.
avoid: Avoid sagging at the hips or losing control of the handles or rings.
Shortened body line: Do not lift the hips first or leave them behind. Raise the support if you cannot move the body together.
Head reach: Do not lead with the chin to imitate more depth. Lower the chest while keeping the neck comfortable.
Loose support: Do not continue on sliding handles or uncontrolled rings. Stabilize the setup or use an easier support.

rope-triceps-pressdown.name: Rope Triceps Pressdown
cues: Set up: Take a secure grip and stabilize your stance or support. Position the upper arm for the intended variation before extending the elbow.
Movement: Set a high cable or band and keep your upper arms near your sides.
Control: Straighten your elbows to press down, then return slowly.
Elbow: Keep the upper arm reasonably steady while the forearm moves. Straighten smoothly without forcing a hard joint stop.
Wrist: Keep the wrist in line with the forearm and the handle secure. Do not substitute wrist movement for elbow extension.
Return: Bend the elbow under control and keep the same upper-arm position. Use resistance that does not drag the shoulder forward.
avoid: Avoid swinging your shoulders or leaning your body weight onto the handle.
Shoulder drive: Do not repeatedly swing the whole arm to move the weight. Reduce resistance and focus on elbow movement.
Bodyweight push: Do not fall onto the handle or lean farther forward with each rep. Keep your base and trunk steady.
Loose return: Do not let the cable or dumbbell pull the elbow back suddenly. Control the return before beginning the next rep.

seated-leg-curl.name: Seated Leg Curl
cues: Set up: Secure the resistance and support your trunk before starting. Try a light repetition to check that the knee can bend freely.
Movement: Align your knee with the machine pivot and secure the pads.
Control: Bend your knee to pull the pad toward you, then return slowly.
Knee movement: Draw the heel toward the back of the thigh while keeping the thigh and pelvis steady against their support.
Range: Curl only as far as you can without lifting your hips or changing your back position; contact with the glutes is not required.
Return: Let the knee extend smoothly while keeping control of the resistance. Maintain secure contact with the pad, cuff or dumbbell.
avoid: Avoid lifting your hips off the support or letting the stack slam.
Back arch: If your lower back arches to finish the curl, reduce resistance and stop the rep before the hips lift.
Rushed return: Do not let the resistance yank the leg straight. Lower slowly enough to keep the knee movement controlled.
Loose contact: Stop if the pad, ankle attachment or dumbbell slips. Reset the attachment instead of trying to catch it mid-rep.

seated-machine-calf-raise.name: Seated Machine Calf Raise
cues: Set up: Secure the support and place the forefoot firmly on the floor or platform. Test your balance before adding resistance.
Movement: Set the thigh pad securely and place the balls of your feet on the platform.
Control: Lift your heels, then lower slowly through a comfortable range.
Ankle path: Raise and lower through the ankle while keeping pressure across the forefoot. Keep the knee angle appropriate to the variation.
Range: If using an elevated platform, lower the heel only as far as you can control. On the floor, return the heel gently to the surface.
Top position: Rise without rolling onto the outer or inner foot edge. Pause briefly and reverse smoothly.
avoid: Avoid bouncing the load or lifting your thighs off the pad.
Bouncing: Do not rebound rapidly out of the bottom stretch. Lower the load and control both directions.
Knee pumping: Do not repeatedly bend and straighten the knees to substitute leg drive for ankle movement.
Foot slipping: Do not continue with only a small toe contact on the edge. Reposition the forefoot and secure the load first.

side-plank.name: Side Plank
cues: Set up: Use a non-slip surface and stack the supporting elbow under the shoulder. Choose full-leg or bent-knee support to suit your control.
Movement: Set your supporting elbow below the shoulder and stack or stagger your feet.
Control: Lift your hips and hold a straight side line while breathing.
Body line: Engage the abdomen and glutes to hold the hips in line with the trunk. Keep the head comfortably aligned.
Shoulder support: Press through the forearm rather than sinking into the shoulder. Keep the supporting hand and elbow steady.
Breathing: Take steady breaths while maintaining the position. End the hold when the body line changes, even before the planned time.
avoid: Avoid letting your hips sag or collapsing onto the shoulder.
Raised hips: Do not lift the hips high to avoid the intended trunk effort. Use an easier support or a shorter hold.
Collapsing shoulder: Do not let the chest sink onto the supporting shoulder. Reset the forearm pressure or reduce difficulty.
Time over control: Do not chase a longer hold with shaking, sagging or a prolonged breath hold. Finish while the position is controlled.

single-leg-calf-raise.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
cues: Set up: Secure the support and place the forefoot firmly on the floor or platform. Test your balance before adding resistance.
Movement: Place the balls of your feet securely on the platform with knees softly straight.
Control: Raise your heels, then lower through a comfortable ankle range.
Ankle path: Raise and lower through the ankle while keeping pressure across the forefoot. Keep the knee angle appropriate to the variation.
Range: If using an elevated platform, lower the heel only as far as you can control. On the floor, return the heel gently to the surface.
Top position: Rise without rolling onto the outer or inner foot edge. Pause briefly and reverse smoothly.
avoid: Avoid bouncing at the bottom or rolling your ankles outward.
Bouncing: Do not rebound rapidly out of the bottom stretch. Lower the load and control both directions.
Knee pumping: Do not repeatedly bend and straighten the knees to substitute leg drive for ankle movement.
Foot slipping: Do not continue with only a small toe contact on the edge. Reposition the forefoot and secure the load first.

standing-barbell-overhead-press.name: Standing Barbell Overhead Press
cues: Set up: Take a full grip and position the load near shoulder height with forearms supporting it. Rehearse the path with light resistance.
Movement: Start with the weight near shoulder height, wrists supported and trunk braced.
Control: Press overhead, then lower back to your comfortable start position.
Brace: Keep ribs over a controlled pelvis as you press. Firm the abdomen without turning the movement into a backward lean.
Shoulders: Let the shoulder blades rotate upward naturally as the arms rise. Do not try to pin them down throughout an overhead press.
Return: Bring the load back along a comfortable, repeatable path. Keep the wrists supported and regain control before the next press.
avoid: Avoid leaning far back or losing balance to finish the rep.
Back compensation: If the ribs flare and you lean far back, reduce the weight or use a supported variation.
Uneven lockout: Do not twist or side-bend to force one arm overhead. Keep the load and range within your control.
Wrist collapse: Do not let the load fold the wrist back while the forearm drifts away underneath it. Adjust grip and resistance.

standing-machine-calf-raise.name: Standing Machine Calf Raise
cues: Set up: Secure the support and place the forefoot firmly on the floor or platform. Test your balance before adding resistance.
Movement: Place the balls of your feet securely on the platform with knees softly straight.
Control: Raise your heels, then lower through a comfortable ankle range.
Ankle path: Raise and lower through the ankle while keeping pressure across the forefoot. Keep the knee angle appropriate to the variation.
Range: If using an elevated platform, lower the heel only as far as you can control. On the floor, return the heel gently to the surface.
Top position: Rise without rolling onto the outer or inner foot edge. Pause briefly and reverse smoothly.
avoid: Avoid bouncing at the bottom or rolling your ankles outward.
Bouncing: Do not rebound rapidly out of the bottom stretch. Lower the load and control both directions.
Knee pumping: Do not repeatedly bend and straighten the knees to substitute leg drive for ankle movement.
Foot slipping: Do not continue with only a small toe contact on the edge. Reposition the forefoot and secure the load first.

straight-bar-cable-triceps-pressdown.name: Straight Bar Cable Triceps Pressdown
cues: Set up: Take a secure grip and stabilize your stance or support. Position the upper arm for the intended variation before extending the elbow.
Movement: Set a high cable or band and keep your upper arms near your sides.
Control: Straighten your elbows to press down, then return slowly.
Elbow: Keep the upper arm reasonably steady while the forearm moves. Straighten smoothly without forcing a hard joint stop.
Wrist: Keep the wrist in line with the forearm and the handle secure. Do not substitute wrist movement for elbow extension.
Return: Bend the elbow under control and keep the same upper-arm position. Use resistance that does not drag the shoulder forward.
avoid: Avoid swinging your shoulders or leaning your body weight onto the handle.
Shoulder drive: Do not repeatedly swing the whole arm to move the weight. Reduce resistance and focus on elbow movement.
Bodyweight push: Do not fall onto the handle or lean farther forward with each rep. Keep your base and trunk steady.
Loose return: Do not let the cable or dumbbell pull the elbow back suddenly. Control the return before beginning the next rep.

trap-bar-deadlift.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
cues: Set up: Bring the load close, take a secure grip and remove slack before lifting. Set the start height so you can brace in balance.
Movement: Set your stance and grip so the weight stays close; brace before lifting.
Control: Push through the floor to stand tall, then lower by bending hips and knees.
Leg drive: Push the floor away as hips and shoulders rise together. Keep the arms long; they hold the load rather than curl it.
Load path: Keep the weight close to your legs while leaving clearance for the knees. Finish standing tall with hips and knees extended.
Reset: Lower with a controlled hip hinge and knee bend. Re-establish your grip, balance and brace before each new pull.
Trap bar: Stand centered inside the frame and grip both handles evenly. Use an appropriate handle height and keep the frame level as you rise.
avoid: Avoid yanking the weight from the floor or leaning back at the top.
Early hip rise: If the hips shoot up while the load stays still, reset your start position and reduce the weight.
Arm pull: Do not bend the elbows or jerk with the shoulders to break the weight free. Build tension before pushing through the legs.
Bouncing: Do not rebound the weight off the floor or rack supports. Settle it and regain control before the next rep.

cable-seated-row.name: Cable Seated Row
cues: Set up: Choose support or a hip-hinge position you can hold for the set. Take a secure grip and test the pulling path with light resistance.
Movement: Set your torso against the support or brace it in a stable position.
Control: Pull the load toward your torso with your elbows, then let your arms extend slowly.
Elbow path: Pull the elbows toward the intended row target while keeping the wrists aligned. Grip width and elbow angle may vary with the exercise.
Shoulder movement: Allow the shoulder blades to glide as the arms reach and pull; do not squeeze them rigidly throughout the rep.
End position: Finish the pull before you have to rock the torso or roll the shoulders forward. Return through the same controlled path.
avoid: Avoid jerking with your trunk or letting the load pull you forward.
Shrugging the pull: Do not raise the shoulders toward the ears to move the handle. Reduce load and restore the intended elbow path.
Changing torso angle: Do not repeatedly stand up or rock backward to finish the row. Use resistance you can pull from a stable base.
Excessive reach: Do not let the returning load pull your whole body out of position. Let the arms reach while retaining trunk control.

dumbbell-seated-shoulder-press.name: Dumbbell Seated Shoulder Press
cues: Set up: Take a full grip and position the load near shoulder height with forearms supporting it. Rehearse the path with light resistance.
Movement: Start with the weight near shoulder height, wrists supported and trunk braced.
Control: Press overhead, then lower back to your comfortable start position.
Brace: Keep ribs over a controlled pelvis as you press. Firm the abdomen without turning the movement into a backward lean.
Shoulders: Let the shoulder blades rotate upward naturally as the arms rise. Do not try to pin them down throughout an overhead press.
Return: Bring the load back along a comfortable, repeatable path. Keep the wrists supported and regain control before the next press.
avoid: Avoid leaning far back or losing balance to finish the rep.
Back compensation: If the ribs flare and you lean far back, reduce the weight or use a supported variation.
Uneven lockout: Do not twist or side-bend to force one arm overhead. Keep the load and range within your control.
Wrist collapse: Do not let the load fold the wrist back while the forearm drifts away underneath it. Adjust grip and resistance.

lever-chest-press.name: Lever Chest Press
cues: Set up: Adjust the seat and start lever so you can grasp the handles without reaching far behind your body. Test the path with a light load.
Movement: Adjust the seat so the handles start near chest height; keep your back supported.
Control: Press the handles forward, then return through a controlled range.
Support: Keep your feet stable and your upper back against the pad. Maintain the same torso position throughout the press.
Hand path: Follow the machine handles with wrists aligned to the forearms. Extend the arms smoothly rather than snapping into the stop.
Return: Let the elbows bend through a comfortable range while keeping the weight stack controlled; use the start-assist lever if provided.
avoid: Avoid lifting your torso off the pad or letting the machine pull you back.
Overlong reach: Do not accept a start position that pulls the shoulders forward off the pad. Adjust the seat or starting range.
Body drive: If your torso leaves the pad or you push hard with the legs to move the handles, lower the selected weight.
Stack drop: Do not relax and let the stack pull the handles back suddenly. Control the final return before releasing your grip.

lever-seated-shoulder-press.name: Lever Seated Shoulder Press
cues: Set up: Take a full grip and position the load near shoulder height with forearms supporting it. Rehearse the path with light resistance.
Movement: Start with the weight near shoulder height, wrists supported and trunk braced.
Control: Press overhead, then lower back to your comfortable start position.
Brace: Keep ribs over a controlled pelvis as you press. Firm the abdomen without turning the movement into a backward lean.
Shoulders: Let the shoulder blades rotate upward naturally as the arms rise. Do not try to pin them down throughout an overhead press.
Return: Bring the load back along a comfortable, repeatable path. Keep the wrists supported and regain control before the next press.
Machine path: Adjust the handles and support to your height. Follow the machine’s arc rather than forcing a free-weight bar path.
avoid: Avoid leaning far back or losing balance to finish the rep.
Back compensation: If the ribs flare and you lean far back, reduce the weight or use a supported variation.
Uneven lockout: Do not twist or side-bend to force one arm overhead. Keep the load and range within your control.
Wrist collapse: Do not let the load fold the wrist back while the forearm drifts away underneath it. Adjust grip and resistance.

bodyweight-rear-lunge.name: Bodyweight Rear Lunge
cues: Set up: Leave enough width between your feet for balance rather than standing on a tightrope. Use light resistance while finding your stride.
Movement: Step backward into a stable stance and lower by bending both knees.
Control: Keep the front foot planted; push through it to return to standing.
Front leg: Keep the front heel and forefoot supported; allow the knee to follow the toes as your hips lower between your feet.
Torso: A controlled forward lean can be appropriate. Keep your trunk braced instead of forcing an upright torso by arching your back.
Balance: Rise mainly through the front leg while the rear leg helps balance. Reset your feet if the next rep starts from an unstable stance.
avoid: Avoid a rushed step or dropping the back knee onto the floor.
Stride mismatch: Do not keep a step length that makes your heel lift or pelvis twist. Adjust the stance before adding weight.
Knee impact: Keep the rear knee from hitting the floor or platform. Shorten the range if you cannot control the last part of the descent.
Uneven reps: Do not rush the less stable side or twist to finish it. Use a controllable load and range on each leg.

walking-lunge.name: Walking Lunge
cues: Set up: Leave enough width between your feet for balance rather than standing on a tightrope. Use light resistance while finding your stride.
Movement: Step forward far enough to stay balanced; lower by bending both knees.
Control: Push through the front leg and bring the next step under control.
Front leg: Keep the front heel and forefoot supported; allow the knee to follow the toes as your hips lower between your feet.
Torso: A controlled forward lean can be appropriate. Keep your trunk braced instead of forcing an upright torso by arching your back.
Balance: Rise mainly through the front leg while the rear leg helps balance. Reset your feet if the next rep starts from an unstable stance.
avoid: Avoid short, hurried steps that make you lose balance.
Stride mismatch: Do not keep a step length that makes your heel lift or pelvis twist. Adjust the stance before adding weight.
Knee impact: Keep the rear knee from hitting the floor or platform. Shorten the range if you cannot control the last part of the descent.
Uneven reps: Do not rush the less stable side or twist to finish it. Use a controllable load and range on each leg.

bodyweight-squat.name: Bodyweight Squat
cues: Set up: Choose a stance and toe angle that let your knees and hips move comfortably. Rehearse the movement before adding load.
Movement: Set your feet at a comfortable width; brace and bend your hips and knees together.
Control: Keep your whole foot planted, squat to a controlled depth, then stand.
Foot pressure: Keep your heel and both sides of the forefoot supported. Let the knees follow the direction of the toes.
Brace: Firm your abdomen before descending and keep the load balanced over your base of support as hips and shoulders rise together.
Depth: Use the deepest repeatable range you can control without losing balance. Knee travel past the toes is not automatically an error.
avoid: Avoid losing foot contact or letting the load pull you out of balance.
Knees collapsing: If the knees suddenly fall inward and the feet roll, reduce the load or depth and rebuild a stable descent.
Rushing the bottom: Do not drop into a depth you cannot reverse under control. Keep tension as you change direction.
Hips shooting up: If your hips rise before your chest and you fold forward, use less resistance and push the floor away evenly.

lever-seated-reverse-fly.name: Lever Seated Reverse Fly
cues: Set up: Use light resistance and stable support. Start with a soft elbow bend and find a shoulder path you can repeat comfortably.
Movement: Support your chest or hinge at the hips with arms hanging below you.
Control: Open your arms to the sides with soft elbows, then return slowly.
Lead: Move the upper arms along the intended raise path rather than flicking the wrists. Keep your neck relaxed.
Shoulder motion: Allow the shoulder blades to move with the arms. Do not force them permanently downward while lifting.
Range: Raise only while the trunk and arm path stay controlled; return deliberately instead of letting the weight fall.
Machine fit: Adjust the seat so the handles or arm pads match your shoulder height. Keep the torso supported and follow the machine’s comfortable arc.
avoid: Avoid turning the fly into a row or lifting by swinging your torso.
Momentum: Do not bounce the knees or swing the torso to start the raise. Lower the resistance and move from the shoulders.
Wrist steering: Do not force the wrists into an exaggerated thumbs-down position. Keep a comfortable grip and wrist alignment.
Changing lever: Do not repeatedly bend the elbows to finish heavy reps. Keep the arm shape consistent or reduce the load.

cable-curl.name: Cable Curl

chest-dip.name: Chest Dip

Control: Bend your elbows to a comfortable depth, then press back up.

avoid: Avoid dropping quickly into a shoulder position you cannot control.

chin-up.name: Chin-up
cues: Set up: Check the bar and arrange a stable way to get on and off it. Use assistance if you cannot control both the pull and descent.
Movement: Hang from a secure bar with a comfortable grip and a braced trunk.
Control: Pull your body toward the bar, then lower with control.
Pull: Think of drawing the elbows down toward the ribs as the body rises. Let the shoulder blades move rather than forcing them still.

Descent: Lower until the arms reach a comfortable extended position while keeping shoulder and grip control.
avoid: Avoid swinging to clear the bar or craning your neck for extra height.

Neck reach: Do not crane the neck just to get the chin over the bar. Keep the head aligned with the moving torso.
Dropping: Do not fall into the bottom or release a failing grip from height. Use a controlled step down and stop before grip failure.

front-plank.name: Front Plank
cues: Set up: Use a non-slip surface and stack the supporting elbow under the shoulder. Choose full-leg or bent-knee support to suit your control.
Movement: Set your forearms under your shoulders and brace your trunk.
Control: Hold a steady line from shoulders to heels while breathing normally.
Body line: Engage the abdomen and glutes to hold the hips in line with the trunk. Keep the head comfortably aligned.
Shoulder support: Press through the forearm rather than sinking into the shoulder. Keep the supporting hand and elbow steady.

avoid: Avoid sagging at the hips or holding your breath.
Raised hips: Do not lift the hips high to avoid the intended trunk effort. Use an easier support or a shorter hold.
Collapsing shoulder: Do not let the chest sink onto the supporting shoulder. Reset the forearm pressure or reduce difficulty.
Time over control: Do not chase a longer hold with shaking, sagging or a prolonged breath hold. Finish while the position is controlled.

cable-standing-fly.name: Cable Standing Fly
cues: Set up: Secure your stance or bench position and select light resistance. Find a comfortable starting arm position before opening wider.
Movement: Set the handles for your chosen fly angle and keep a small bend at the elbows.
Control: Bring your arms together in front of your chest, then open slowly.
Arm arc: Keep a small, fairly consistent elbow bend as the upper arms move. Think of bringing the arms together rather than pushing the hands.

avoid: Avoid turning the fly into a press or stretching past shoulder control.
Changing elbow bend: Do not repeatedly bend and straighten the elbows to turn the fly into a press. Lower the resistance if needed.
Forced bottom: Do not let gravity or the cable pull the arms farther back than you can reverse smoothly.
Torso swing: Do not rock your body or lift off the support to close the arms. Restore a stable setup with less load.

sled-hack-squat.name: Sled Hack Squat
cues: Set up: Adjust the back and shoulder supports to fit you. Find the safety stops and release mechanism before moving the load.
Movement: Set the seat or pads to fit the machine; keep your feet stable on the platform.
Control: Bend hips and knees through a comfortable range, then press to stand.
Feet: Place the whole foot securely on the platform. Choose spacing that lets the knees follow the feet throughout the machine path.
Range: Stop the descent before your pelvis rolls away from the pad or your feet lose support; more depth is not useful without control.

avoid: Avoid lifting your heels or forcing the machine past your controlled range.
Hands pushing knees: Keep hands on the machine grips instead of using your arms to force a rep. Reduce the resistance when needed.
Uneven pressure: Do not let one foot slide or one leg take over. Reset your stance before continuing.
Uncontrolled release: Do not unlock a sled you cannot support or continue when you cannot reach its catches. Test the mechanism with a light load.

dumbbell-glute-bridge.name: Dumbbell Glute Bridge
cues: Set up: Choose secure support and foot placement that let you lift without sliding. Center and stabilize any external load before starting.
Movement: Lie on your back with feet planted and the load secure over your hips.
Control: Lift your hips by pressing through your feet; lower with control.
Hip drive: Press the feet down and lift from the hips. Keep your ribs from flaring as the pelvis rises.

avoid: Avoid arching your lower back to gain extra height.
Sliding support: Do not continue if the bench, back support or feet shift. Unload and reposition the setup first.
Head thrown back: Keep the neck comfortable rather than throwing your head backward to finish the lift.
Uneven hips: If one side rises or twists first, reduce the load or range and restore an even, controlled hip movement.

avoid: Avoid yanking the weight from the floor or leaning back at the top.

Arm pull: Do not bend the elbows or jerk with the shoulders to break the weight free. Build tension before pushing through the legs.
Bouncing: Do not rebound the weight off the floor or rack supports. Settle it and regain control before the next rep.

Control: Keep your whole foot planted, squat to a controlled depth, then stand.

avoid: Avoid losing foot contact or letting the load pull you out of balance.
Knees collapsing: If the knees suddenly fall inward and the feet roll, reduce the load or depth and rebuild a stable descent.
Rushing the bottom: Do not drop into a depth you cannot reverse under control. Keep tension as you change direction.
Hips shooting up: If your hips rise before your chest and you fold forward, use less resistance and push the floor away evenly.

avoid: Avoid bouncing the weight or losing control of your shoulder position.
Grip mismatch: Do not force a grip width that makes the wrists fold or shoulders uncomfortable. Adjust the grip with a light load first.
Changing support: Do not lift your pelvis or slide along the support to complete a difficult rep. Stop before the position breaks down.

Forced bottom: Do not let gravity or the cable pull the arms farther back than you can reverse smoothly.
Torso swing: Do not rock your body or lift off the support to close the arms. Restore a stable setup with less load.

Trunk: Keep the abdomen firm and ribs controlled. In a single-arm press, let the shoulder move without turning the whole torso.
Return: Guide the end back toward the same shoulder position. Keep your balance and hand contact until the load is parked.
avoid: Avoid twisting your torso or leaning back to finish the press.
Loose anchor: Do not press with a bar end sliding around the floor. Use a secure anchor and check it before loading.
Body turn: Do not rotate or lean to finish a heavy rep. Use less resistance and a stable stance.
Overreach: Do not chase extra reach by arching the lower back. Finish within shoulder and trunk control.

lever-lateral-raise.name: Lever Lateral Raise
cues: Set up: Use light resistance and stable support. Start with a soft elbow bend and find a shoulder path you can repeat comfortably.
Movement: Start with your arms low and elbows softly bent.
Control: Raise your arms out to a comfortable shoulder height, then lower slowly.
Lead: Move the upper arms along the intended raise path rather than flicking the wrists. Keep your neck relaxed.
Shoulder motion: Allow the shoulder blades to move with the arms. Do not force them permanently downward while lifting.
Range: Raise only while the trunk and arm path stay controlled; return deliberately instead of letting the weight fall.
avoid: Avoid using an exaggerated neck shrug or torso swing to lift the load.
Momentum: Do not bounce the knees or swing the torso to start the raise. Lower the resistance and move from the shoulders.
Wrist steering: Do not force the wrists into an exaggerated thumbs-down position. Keep a comfortable grip and wrist alignment.
Changing lever: Do not repeatedly bend the elbows to finish heavy reps. Keep the arm shape consistent or reduce the load.

cable-seated-rear-delt-fly-with-chest-su.name: Cable Seated Rear Delt Fly with Chest Support
cues: Set up: Use light resistance and stable support. Start with a soft elbow bend and find a shoulder path you can repeat comfortably.
Movement: Support your chest or hinge at the hips with arms hanging below you.
Control: Open your arms to the sides with soft elbows, then return slowly.
Lead: Move the upper arms along the intended raise path rather than flicking the wrists. Keep your neck relaxed.
Shoulder motion: Allow the shoulder blades to move with the arms. Do not force them permanently downward while lifting.
Range: Raise only while the trunk and arm path stay controlled; return deliberately instead of letting the weight fall.
avoid: Avoid turning the fly into a row or lifting by swinging your torso.
Momentum: Do not bounce the knees or swing the torso to start the raise. Lower the resistance and move from the shoulders.
Wrist steering: Do not force the wrists into an exaggerated thumbs-down position. Keep a comfortable grip and wrist alignment.
Changing lever: Do not repeatedly bend the elbows to finish heavy reps. Keep the arm shape consistent or reduce the load.

barbell-upright-row.name: Barbell Upright Row
cues: Set up: Stand balanced with a full grip and the load close to the body. Select light resistance while finding a comfortable shoulder path.
Movement: Hold the bar or dumbbells in front of your thighs with a comfortable grip.
Control: Lead with your elbows as you raise the load to a comfortable height; lower slowly.
Path: Lift smoothly along the exercise’s intended path. Keep the head level rather than pushing the chin forward.
Range: Finish within a comfortable shoulder range; a higher end position is not required if it changes your grip or trunk control.
Return: Lower under control with the trunk steady and keep the same path on successive repetitions.
avoid: Avoid forcing your shoulders into a painful range or shrugging to finish.
Body heave: Do not use a knee bounce or backward lean to lift the load. Reduce the weight and move deliberately.
Wrist strain: Do not force a grip that folds the wrists awkwardly. Adjust spacing or use a more comfortable handle.
Neck tension: Do not thrust the head forward or circle the neck to exaggerate the lift. Keep it aligned with the torso.

barbell-curl.name: Barbell Curl
cues: Set up: Choose the intended grip and secure any bench or arm support. Start with resistance you can curl without moving the trunk.
Movement: Keep your upper arms near your torso and hold the load with steady wrists.
Control: Bend your elbows to lift the load, then lower with control.
Elbow movement: Bend at the elbow while keeping the upper arm reasonably steady in the position for this variation.
Wrist: Keep the wrist aligned with the forearm. Any grip rotation should be deliberate rather than caused by the weight pulling your hand.
Return: Extend the elbow smoothly through a comfortable range. Retain control near the bottom rather than dropping into the stretch.
avoid: Avoid swinging your torso to move the weight.
Trunk swing: Do not lean back or drive with the hips to start the curl. Lower the load and keep the same support position.
Elbow drift: Do not let the upper arm suddenly travel forward to finish heavy reps. Use a range and load you can control.
Bottom bounce: Do not rebound out of an extended elbow, especially on a supported curl. Slow the last part of the return.

ez-barbell-spider-curl.name: EZ Barbell Spider Curl
cues: Set up: Choose the intended grip and secure any bench or arm support. Start with resistance you can curl without moving the trunk.
Movement: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with arms hanging freely.
Control: Curl the weight without lifting your chest, then lower slowly.
Elbow movement: Bend at the elbow while keeping the upper arm reasonably steady in the position for this variation.
Wrist: Keep the wrist aligned with the forearm. Any grip rotation should be deliberate rather than caused by the weight pulling your hand.

Spider support: Keep the chest on the incline bench and let the upper arms hang. Curl without lifting the chest to meet the weights.
avoid: Avoid swinging the arms or peeling your torso off the pad.

Elbow movement: Bend at the elbow while keeping the upper arm reasonably steady in the position for this variation.

lever-preacher-curl.name: Lever Preacher Curl
cues: Set up: Choose the intended grip and secure any bench or arm support. Start with resistance you can curl without moving the trunk.
Movement: Rest your upper arms on the pad and keep your wrists steady.
Control: Curl the load, then lower until your elbows are comfortably extended.
Elbow movement: Bend at the elbow while keeping the upper arm reasonably steady in the position for this variation.
Wrist: Keep the wrist aligned with the forearm. Any grip rotation should be deliberate rather than caused by the weight pulling your hand.
